title: ASEAN Guide on AI Governance and Ethics
summary: Endorsed at the 4th ASEAN Digital Ministers' Meeting in Singapore. Sets national and regional recommendations with a voluntary, market-driven approach.

title: ASEAN Working Group on AI Governance (WG-AI)
summary: Working group formed to drive the guide's recommendations and serve as ASEAN's focal point on AI with outside partners.
notes: Month taken from a law-firm guide; confirm against an ASEAN source.

title: Expanded ASEAN Guide on AI Governance and Ethics: Generative AI
summary: Adds nine policy recommendations on generative AI and covers deepfakes, impersonation and fraud among six named risks. Adoption by member states is voluntary.

title: Hanoi Digital Declaration (6th ASEAN Digital Ministers' Meeting)
summary: Includes AI commitments: deeper policy harmonisation and joint safety efforts under the WG-AI. It is a general commitment and does not address the Grok case specifically.

title: Model AI Governance Framework (1st edition)
summary: Singapore's first voluntary, sector-agnostic framework for responsible AI, released for consultation and adoption.

title: Model AI Governance Framework (2nd edition)
summary: Adds robustness and reproducibility considerations and refines the first edition for usability.

title: National AI Strategy (NAIS 1.0)
summary: Singapore's first national AI strategy.

title: AI Verify testing framework and toolkit (international pilot)
summary: A governance testing framework and open-source toolkit for checking AI systems against 11 internationally recognised principles.

title: National AI Strategy 2.0 (NAIS 2.0)
summary: Updates the 2019 strategy, treating AI as a necessity and committing to a trusted environment alongside capability building.

title: Model AI Governance Framework for Generative AI
summary: Sets out nine dimensions for trustworthy generative AI, after public consultation from January to March 2024.

title: Elections (Integrity of Online Advertising) (Amendment) Act 2024
summary: Prohibits publishing, boosting, sharing or reposting deepfakes and other digitally manipulated content depicting election candidates, and lets candidates seek review and corrective directions. Introduced 9 Sep 2024, passed 15 Oct 2024.

title: Online Safety (Relief and Accountability) Act
summary: Passed 5 Nov 2025 after introduction on 15 Oct 2025. Creates an Online Safety Commission able to direct takedowns, restrict perpetrator accounts and help victims identify anonymous perpetrators. Partial commencement 29 June 2026: OSC began operations and specified statutory-tort provisions took effect.
next_milestone: Remaining OSRAA provisions / harm categories progressively brought into effect
notes: Partial commencement 29 Jun 2026 only: OSC operational and specified statutory-tort provisions in effect; first phase covers intimate image abuse, image-based child abuse, doxxing, online harassment, online stalking. Commissioner Francis Ng from 29 Jun 2026.

title: Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI
summary: Unveiled by the Minister for Digital Development and Information at the World Economic Forum in Davos. Treats agency as a transfer of decision rights to a system.

title: Criminal Law (Miscellaneous Amendments) Act 2025
summary: Passed 4 Nov 2025 (first read 14 Oct 2025). Extends 'intimate image' to synthetic AI-generated material; new offence of producing intimate images without consent, including AI-generated; clarifies child abuse material covers computer-generated material. AI provisions in force 17 Aug 2026.
next_milestone: Remaining provisions brought into force
notes: Passed 4 Nov 2025. First tranche in force 30 Dec 2025; AI/intimate-image tranche in force 17 Aug 2026; remaining provisions to follow.

title: National Strategy for AI 2020-2045 (Stranas KA)
summary: National AI strategy covering ethics and policy; a presidential regulation on AI is meant to build on it.

title: Personal Data Protection Law (Law No. 27/2022)
summary: Indonesia's general data protection statute, one of the laws used to oversee AI in the absence of an AI-specific law.
notes: Enacted and in force 17 Oct 2022 (Pasal 76; LN 2022/196). Two-year conformity period under Pasal 74 ended 17 Oct 2024. Implementing regulation PP 33/2026 (see ID-P-06) takes effect 16 Jan 2027; dedicated supervisory agency not yet established as of Nov 2026.

title: Ministry Circular Letter No. 9/2023 on AI Ethics
summary: Sets ethical principles for AI, including inclusivity, security and transparency. Compliance is not mandatory.

title: Electronic Information and Transactions (ITE) Law, as amended (2024)
summary: Core law on electronic information, one of the existing laws to which penalties for AI misuse currently refer.

title: Draft Presidential Regulations on AI Ethics and the National AI Roadmap 2026–2029
issuer: Ministry of Communication and Digital Affairs
summary: Two draft Presidential Regulations prepared by Komdigi after public consultation 8–22 Aug 2025: one on AI ethics (three risk tiers, no sanctions of its own) and one on the National AI Roadmap 2026–2029 (10 focus sectors). Harmonisation completed Apr 2026; both drafts initialled by ministers and awaiting President Prabowo's signature as of 11 Nov 2026. No Perpres number issued. Minister told DPR 26 Jan 2026 that signature in 2026 was the priority.
next_milestone: Presidential signature of both Perpres
notes: Roadmap period is 2026–2029, not 2025–2030. A 30 Oct 2026 report said the drafts were 'now being signed'; as of 11 Nov 2026 they were still awaiting the President's signature and no Perpres number exists.

title: National Guidelines on AI Governance and Ethics
issuer: Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (MOSTI)
summary: Non-binding guidance encouraging developers and deployers to adopt responsible AI practices voluntarily.

title: National AI Office (NAIO) launched
summary: Agency set up to accelerate adoption and shape AI policy and governance; widely seen as the lead on AI regulation.
notes: NAIO's own site gives an earlier establishment date (28 August); the launch is dated 12 December 2024. Institutionalised as AI Malaysia Berhad, announced by PM Anwar Ibrahim 28 July 2026; AI Malaysia Berhad now leads national AI coordination.

title: Licensing of social media and messaging platforms (8 million+ users)
summary: Platforms with at least eight million users in Malaysia must hold an application service provider class licence. Reports say X fell below that threshold and was exempt.

title: Online Safety Act 2025 (Act 866)
summary: Passed by Parliament in December 2024, royal assent 6 May 2025, in force 1 Jan 2026 with age-verification duties and subsidiary regulations. The minister has used its instruments against deepfake scam ads.
notes: One law-firm note dates the passage to December 2025; the legislative timeline above indicates December 2024.

title: Proposed AI Governance Bill: public consultation paper
summary: Consultation paper for what would be Malaysia's first horizontal AI statute, covering AI across sectors. Submissions closed 31 July 2026 (317 submissions from 218 entities); draft Bill completed by Sep 2026. Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo told the Dewan Rakyat 29 Oct 2026 the Bill will go to Cabinet and is targeted for tabling by early 2027 — the earlier 2026 tabling expectation has slipped. Bill text not yet published.
next_milestone: Bill tabled in Parliament (government target: early 2027)

title: Law on Digital Technology Industry (Law No. 71/2025/QH15)
summary: The first Vietnamese law to explicitly mention AI, treating it as a strategic technology. Some articles took effect 1 July 2025. Its AI provisions were later replaced by the Law on AI.

title: Law on Personal Data Protection
summary: Vietnam's first dedicated personal-data statute, effective 1 Jan 2026 alongside implementing Decree 356/2025/ND-CP.
notes: Law 91/2025/QH15 and Decree 356/2025/ND-CP repealed Decree 13/2023/ND-CP with effect from 1 Jan 2026.

title: Law on Artificial Intelligence (Law No. 134/2025/QH15)
summary: Passed 10 Dec 2025 (429 of 434 votes) and in effect 1 Mar 2026. A risk-based, standalone statute described as the first binding AI law in Southeast Asia. National security and defence uses are carved out.

title: Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012 (RA 10175)
summary: General cybercrime statute. Authorities ordered the 2026 Grok takedown under it. It was not written for AI deepfakes.
notes: Year of enactment taken from general knowledge; confirm against the statute text.

title: Data Privacy Act of 2012 (RA 10173)
summary: Foundation of data protection law and one of the cornerstones of the current AI governance regime alongside the national AI strategy.
notes: Year of enactment taken from general knowledge; confirm against the statute text.

title: National AI Strategy Roadmap 1.0
summary: First roadmap, focused on industrial competitiveness.

title: National AI Strategy Roadmap 2.0
summary: Updated roadmap adopted after the rapid emergence of generative AI.
source_title: DTI: DTI launches National AI Strategy Roadmap 2.0 and Center for AI Research
notes: Exact month verified (see backlog). DTI is reported to now label NAISR 2.0 an archived reference following NAIS-PH — confirm against a DTI source before changing status from in_force.

title: National AI Strategy for the Philippines (NAIS-PH)
issuer: Department of Science and Technology; approved by the Office of the President
summary: Presidential strategy approved by President Marcos Jr., described as the cornerstone of the current regime. Approved by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. at a sectoral meeting on 20 May 2025; five pillars (infrastructure, workforce, innovation, ethics/policy, deployment), phased 2024–2028.
source_title: OpenGov Asia: The Philippines: President Approves Comprehensive AI Roadmap

title: COMELEC Resolution No. 11064: AI and social media in election campaigns
summary: Regulates AI and social media in digital campaigns for the May 2025 elections: requires disclosure of AI use in campaign material and penalises misuse for disinformation.
notes: Written for the 2025 elections; applicability to later polls to confirm.

title: House Bill 10567: Deepfake Accountability and Transparency Act
summary: Would regulate AI-generated deepfakes with disclosure requirements. Pending in committee; reported as under review as of September 2026.
next_milestone: Refile/substitute bill (HB 6314 or HB 7584) progress in the 20th Congress
notes: Pending in the Committee on Information and Communications Technology in the 19th Congress; no committee report or floor vote found. The 19th Congress ended 30 June 2025, so the bill lapsed; no refile under HB 10567 found in the 20th Congress. Successor deepfake work: HB 6314 (Fake News and Digital Disinformation Act) and HB 7584 (filed 3 Feb 2026, pending ICT since 9 Feb 2026).

title: Thailand National AI Strategy and Action Plan (2022-2027)
issuer: Cabinet of Thailand; Ministry of Digital Economy and Society
summary: Five-pillar plan covering ethical, legal and regulatory readiness, infrastructure, skills, research and sector adoption. A Prime Minister-chaired national AI committee was set up in August 2022.
source_title: Tilleke & Gibbins, 'Comprehensive Policy: Thailand's AI Governance Framework'

title: Digital Thailand AI Ethics Guideline (2022)
issuer: Digital Thailand (Ministry of Digital Economy and Society)
summary: Non-binding national guideline setting out six ethical principles for regulators, developers, providers and users of AI.
notes: Sources give 1 March 2022 and 22 March 2022 for different guideline entries, so year precision is used. The issuer is named at ministry level only.

title: Emergency Decree on Prevention and Suppression of Technological Crimes B.E. 2566 (2023), as amended in April 2025
summary: The April 2025 amendment, published in the Government Gazette on 12 April, set up a Center for Prevention and Suppression of Technology Crimes that can notify financial institutions of names and wallet addresses linked to technology crime. The final text dropped an earlier proposal to widen the definition to cover forged identity and biometrics.
notes: The original decree dates from 2023; this entry records the 2025 amendment. Law-firm bulletin; the Gazette text was not opened.

title: Notification of the Electronic Transactions Commission on Measures to Prevent Technological Crimes for Social Media Service Providers
summary: Issued under the amended Emergency Decree and in effect from 5 July 2025, it sets duties for social media platforms aimed at online fraud and technology-related crime.
notes: Law-firm bulletin; the notification text was not opened. Its specific duties are not summarised here.

title: National Cyber Security Agency AI security guidelines
summary: Recommendations for protecting AI systems from cyber threats, aligned with ISO/IEC 42001:2023 and the NIST AI risk framework.
source_title: Tilleke & Gibbins, Thailand's AI governance framework
notes: Month precision from a law-firm summary.

title: Draft Act on Artificial Intelligence (ETDA public hearing)
summary: New draft released for a public hearing of about 30 days. It would apply to AI development or deployment affecting people in Thailand, even from abroad; high-risk AI would be designated by royal decree; it adds a regulatory sandbox. An earlier set of draft principles had a hearing in May and June 2025.
source_title: Tilleke & Gibbins, 'Thailand releases new draft AI Act'
next_milestone: Outcome of the public hearing and a revised draft
notes: Law-firm summary; the draft text was not opened. Whether it names deepfakes was not checked.

title: Memorandum of agreement among the DOJ, PCO and DICT against disinformation and deepfakes
issuer: Department of Justice; Presidential Communications Office; Department of ICT
summary: Signed 13 April 2026 at DOJ Manila by PCO Acting Secretary Dave M. Gomez, DICT Secretary Henry R. Aguda and Acting DOJ Secretary Frederick A. Vida under 'Oplan Kontra Fake News'. The PCO leads public information, the DOJ legal enforcement, and the DICT technology, cybersecurity and monitoring. The Justice Secretary said the government will distinguish criminal disinformation from protected speech.
source_title: PCO/PIA: PCO, DICT, DOJ forge pact vs fake news, deepfakes
next_milestone: Primary release and any implementing guidelines
notes: Signing date verified as 13 Apr 2026 from the PIA republication of the PCO release. Exact PCO page URL not recovered; PIA URL used as the primary-government source.

title: Declaration on the Establishment of an ASEAN AI Safety Network (ASEAN AI SAFE)
summary: Leaders agreed to set up a regional network supporting the Digital Senior Officials' Meeting and the Working Group on AI Governance on AI safety. It operates on a voluntary and non-binding basis and acknowledges cross-border AI risks such as misinformation, fraud and content manipulation. Digital ministers adopted it in January 2026, and a Kuala Lumpur secretariat was announced.
notes: Names fraud and content manipulation generally, not deepfakes, so names_risk is no.

title: ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement (DEFA)
summary: Signed in Manila on 14 November 2026 after negotiations that began in September 2023. Reported to cover digital trade, cross-border data flows, payments, cybersecurity and cooperation on AI, and described as the first legally binding standalone digital economy agreement in the region.
next_milestone: Entry into force and implementation plan (reports differ: first projects in early 2027, or 180 days after signing)
notes: Placed in the online-safety layer for its cybersecurity cooperation, though it is a broad digital-economy agreement. The signed text was not reviewed, so whether the AI provisions bind states or only commit them to cooperate is unconfirmed.

title: Protection from Online Falsehoods and Manipulation Act 2019
summary: General falsehoods law enabling authorities to act against deliberate online falsehoods, including through correction directions. Administered by IMDA through the POFMA Office. Can apply to deepfake falsehoods but does not name deepfakes or AI.
notes: Does not name deepfakes or AI; included as the general falsehoods regime applicable to deepfake falsehoods.

title: Online Criminal Harms Act 2023
summary: Enables directions, orders and information powers against online criminal activity, especially scams and malicious cyber activity. Directions/orders/information powers in force 1 Feb 2024; codes-of-practice provisions 24 Jun 2024. Police have said OCHA directions can be used against deepfake impersonation-scam content whether or not AI-generated.
source_title: MHA: Commencement of OCHA on 1 February 2024
notes: Does not name deepfakes in its text; deepfake-fraud theme reflects its use against deepfake impersonation scams.

title: Code of Practice for Online Safety – Social Media Services
summary: Issued under s.45L Broadcasting Act 1994 for designated social media services (Facebook, HardwareZone, Instagram, TikTok, X, YouTube). Requires measures to minimise exposure to harmful content, including sexual content, with enhanced protections for children. The instrument IMDA cited when engaging X over Grok misuse.
source_title: IMDA: Code of Practice for Online Safety – Social Media Services
notes: Does not name deepfakes or AI. A separate IMDA PDF of a general Code of Practice for Online Safety 2023 states 28 Jun 2023; 18 Jul 2023 is the Social Media Services version used here.

title: Government Regulation No. 33 of 2026 on the Implementation of Personal Data Protection
summary: Implementing regulation for the PDP Law (UU 27/2022): DPIA for automated decisions and new technology, Data Protection Officer duties, 3x24-hour breach notice, right to object to automated processing. Promulgated 16 July 2026 (State Gazette 2026 No. 88); takes effect 16 January 2027.
source_title: Recording Law: Indonesia PDP Law vs GDPR
notes: Sources differ by a day on promulgation (mid-July 2026); 16 July 2026 is used per State Gazette No. 88. Effective date 16 Jan 2027 per Pasal 225.

title: Malaysia National Artificial Intelligence Roadmap 2021-2025 (AI-RMAP)
issuer: Ministry of Science Technology and Innovation (MOSTI)
summary: Malaysia's first structured national AI framework: governance, R&D, infrastructure, talent, social adoption and innovation ecosystem, with seven responsible-AI principles and national use cases in five priority sectors. Superseded by the National AI Action Plan 2026-2030, launched 28 July 2026.
notes: Launch month March 2021 per UKM journal and US-ASEAN/KRI reports; Digital Policy Alert and AIPolicyTracker cite adoption on 1 Dec 2021 and note the exact date is not stated on official pages. Month precision used.

title: National AI Action Plan 2026-2030 (AI Nation 2030)
issuer: Ministry of Digital; AI Malaysia Berhad
summary: Five-year implementation blueprint for AI Nation 2030: 14 sectoral (Impact Engine) initiatives and 14 enabler initiatives under five enablers including Responsible Governance. Launched 28 July 2026 by PM Anwar Ibrahim alongside AI Malaysia Berhad (institutionalisation of NAIO) and the Malaysia AI Safety Institute. Successor to the AI Roadmap 2021-2025.
source_title: Ministry of Digital: AI Malaysia announcement

title: Artificial Intelligence Systems Cyber Security Framework (AISCF)
summary: Risk-based framework for securing AI systems across a seven-phase lifecycle (inception to retirement), applying secure-by-design and defence-in-depth across AI data, models, and infrastructure/applications. Launched by PM Anwar Ibrahim at the National Cyber Security Summit 2026, Putrajaya, with the National Cryptography Policy. Voluntary reference, not mandatory.
notes: Launch date 9 July 2026 from a taskforce contributor's record and summit coverage; NACSA's own PDF is undated in the excerpts checked. NACSA chief said pre-launch (Apr 2026) the guidelines would be a reference, not mandatory.

title: Risk Mitigation Code (RMC) under the Online Safety Act 2025
summary: Code under s.80 of the Online Safety Act 2025 (s.13 duties): licensed service providers must run harmful-content risk assessments, strengthen content governance, reporting and response, verify advertisers, and label manipulated content. Published 22 May 2026 after public consultation 12 Feb-31 Mar 2026; in effect 1 June 2026. Non-compliance can draw fines up to RM10 million.
source_title: Lexology: ONSA Child Protection Code and Risk Mitigation Code Published
notes: names_risk=yes because the Code expressly requires labelling of manipulated/AI-generated media. Enforcement from 1 June 2026 with a grace period for verification processes.

title: Child Protection Code (CPC) under the Online Safety Act 2025
summary: Code under s.80 of the Online Safety Act 2025 (s.18 duties): licensed service providers must protect child users, including age verification so only users 16+ may register, safety-by-design and age-appropriate defaults. Published 22 May 2026 after public consultation 12 Feb-31 Mar 2026; in effect 1 June 2026.
source_title: Lexology: ONSA Child Protection Code and Risk Mitigation Code Published

title: National Strategy on Research Development and Application of Artificial Intelligence through 2030 (Decision No. 127/QD-TTg)
summary: Vietnam's national AI strategy, promulgated by Prime Minister's Decision 127/QD-TTg. Targets top-4 in ASEAN and top-50 globally in AI research development and application by 2030, with three national big-data and high-performance computing centres, national AI innovation centres and open datasets. Directs work on a legal framework, infrastructure, talent and AI application; the Ministry of Science and Technology is the focal point for implementation. Non-binding strategy; the binding Law on AI followed in 2025.
notes: Signed by Deputy Prime Minister Vu Duc Dam on behalf of the Prime Minister. Takes effect from the date of signing. Superseded by Decision 1671/QĐ-TTg (National Strategy on Artificial Intelligence to 2030, vision to 2045), approved 28 Aug 2026 — see VN-P-07.

title: Decree No. 13/2023/ND-CP on Personal Data Protection
summary: Vietnam's first comprehensive personal data protection decree, effective 1 July 2023. Repealed with effect from 1 January 2026 by the Law on Personal Data Protection (No. 91/2025/QH15) and its implementing Decree No. 356/2025/ND-CP.
source_title: Medibase — Personal Data Protection in Vietnamese Digital

title: Decree No. 356/2025/ND-CP detailing implementation of the Law on Personal Data Protection
summary: Implementing decree for the Law on Personal Data Protection (No. 91/2025/QH15), issued 31 December 2025 and effective 1 January 2026. Expressly repealed Decree 13/2023/ND-CP.
notes: Also consider adding a note to VN-P-02 that Law 91/2025/QH15 repealed Decree 13 from 1 Jan 2026.

title: Personal Data Protection Act B.E. 2562 (2019)
issuer: National Legislative Assembly / Government of Thailand
summary: Thailand's general data-protection statute, modelled on the GDPR. Published in the Royal Gazette 27 May 2019; fully effective 1 June 2022 after repeated postponements. Thai PBS Verify cites it as prohibiting use of personal data such as face, name and voice without consent, making it one of the laws covering deepfakes.
notes: Gazette text not opened; PDPC enforcement record not checked.

title: Computer-Related Crime Act B.E. 2550 (2007) as amended by Act (No. 2) B.E. 2560 (2017)
summary: Core cybercrime statute used against false/distorted computer data. Section 14 covers dishonestly entering distorted or false computer data; Section 16 (as amended 2017) specifically covers doctored images of another person likely to cause reputational harm (up to 3 years / 200,000 baht). Thai PBS Verify lists it as the current law regulating deepfakes in Thailand.
notes: Year precision used for original enactment (2007); exact 2017 amendment publication date not verified. The Act does not name AI or deepfakes, so names_risk is no.

title: ASEAN Responsible AI Roadmap 2025-2030
summary: Adopted 5 March 2025 by all 10 ASEAN states. Gives policymakers customized, step-by-step guidance to operationalise responsible AI in an integrated and interoperable way, across four pillars: internal governance; skills and knowledge; risk mitigation and monitoring; stakeholder coordination and regional cooperation. Non-binding.
next_milestone: Implementation progress check
notes: Distinct from ASEAN-P-05 (AI Safety Network declaration). The ASEAN book page itself carries no date; the 5 Mar 2025 adoption date comes from Digital Policy Alert and Drew & Napier.

title: ASEAN Leaders' Declaration on AI-Powered MSME Growth
summary: Adopted 15 November 2026 in Manila. Sets a coordinated regional vision for AI adoption by MSMEs, with voluntary AI governance in line with national laws, lawful and ethical AI use, transparency, accountability, cybersecurity, data governance, human oversight, personal data protection for MSMEs and IP respect. Guided by the 2024 AI Guide, the Expanded GenAI Guide and the Responsible AI Roadmap. Philippines, as lead proponent, to report on the AI-Powered MSME Growth Action Plan.
next_milestone: Philippines' progress report on the Action Plan
notes: Outcome of the ASEAN AI Summit on AI-Powered MSME Growth, held virtually 6 October 2026 (not Cebu, September, as originally framed). The summit was announced at the 48th ASEAN Summit in Cebu, 5-8 May 2026.

title: Japan-ASEAN AI Safety and Security Partnership
issuer: Japan and ASEAN Member States (29th ASEAN-Japan Summit)
summary: Launched by Japan at the 29th ASEAN-Japan Summit in Manila. Voluntary, non-binding cooperation on AI safety, security, governance and assurance, focused on sharing best practices and information and capacity-building, in coordination with the ASEAN Working Group on AI Governance and the ASEAN AI Safety Network. Covers model testing, technical expertise and government evaluation capability, against risks including cybersecurity threats and loss of human control.
next_milestone: Work programme / budget / timetable
notes: No budget, staffing or timetable published yet. Distinct from the Japan-ASEAN Co-creation Initiative for AI mentioned in the same summit.

title: Draft National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2025–2030
summary: Six strategic priorities and 41 strategic measures to make Cambodia a skilful adopter of AI in the short term and a participant in the AI development market in the long term, covering human resources, data/infrastructure, AI for digital government, sectoral adoption, ethical and responsible AI, and collaboration/research/innovation.
next_milestone: Submit to the Digital Government Committee and National Digital Economy and Society Council for review and approval (MPTC workplan, April 2025)
notes: Public consultation ran to 20 June 2025; national workshop held 1 July 2025. Formal approval not verified by October 2026 (Digital Watch Observatory) and PM Hun Manet on 17 July 2026 still described adoption as forthcoming, so status stays draft.

title: Draft Law on Personal Data Protection
summary: Cambodia's first comprehensive personal data protection framework, GDPR-style: data-subject rights including human review of automated decisions, mandatory certified data protection officers, data protection impact assessments for high-risk processing, 72-hour breach notification, cross-border transfer controls, and fines up to 600 million riel (about USD 150,000) or 10% of annual turnover, with a two-year implementation period after promulgation.
next_milestone: Enactment (promulgation); two-year implementation period to follow
notes: Third draft issued 23 July 2025; consultative workshop held that day with about 200 participants. Still a draft at the MPTC validation workshop on 5 August 2026.

title: Law on Combating Technology-Enabled Scams
summary: Five chapters and 24 articles creating five new offences: technology-enabled fraud; organising or leading a scam centre; recruiting or training others to commit such fraud; maliciously collecting personal identification documents or information; and a specific form of money laundering. Penalties up to life imprisonment, fines up to 1 billion riel (about USD 250,000) and asset seizure. Promulgated by Royal Kram No. NS/RKM/0426/006; National Assembly passed 30 March 2026, Senate approved 3 April 2026, effective on promulgation.
notes: Title variants in secondary sources: 'Law on Combating Technology-Based Fraud' and 'Law on Anti-Technology Fraud'. AI is mentioned only in the minister's dissemination remarks (officials must understand new tactics 'including the use of AI'); the law text as summarised does not contain an AI-specific provision, so themes rest on technology-enabled fraud generally.

title: Law on Prevention and Combating Cyber Crime (No. 61/NA)
short_title: Law on Prevention and Combating Cyber Crime
issuer: National Assembly of the Lao PDR
summary: Criminalises cyber offences including unauthorised access to computer systems, unauthorised editing of content, photos, video and sound, causing loss through online social media, dissemination of pornography through computer systems, and computer data forgery; establishes LaoCERT as the national computer emergency response team.
source_title: Unofficial translation, National Assembly (via Ministry of Industry and Commerce)
notes: KPL (Oct 2026) says the original law was 'adopted in August 2015'; 15 July 2015 is the date on the law text and per Tilleke & Gibbins and the Council of Europe profile. Promulgated by presidential decree No. 135/PDT on 28 Aug 2015.

title: Law on Electronic Data Protection (No. 25/NA)
issuer: National Assembly of the Lao PDR
summary: Governs the collection, processing and protection of electronic data; classifies data as general or personal/specific, requires consent of the data owner for collection, use or disclosure of specific data, requires Data Administrator consent for cross-border transfer, and designates the Ministry of Technology and Communications as the responsible authority.
notes: Date and number agreed by Digital Watch, Tilleke & Gibbins/Multilaw, CaseGuard and JD Supra. An ASEAN ATRC meeting report (Oct 2024) refers to a 'Law on Electronic Data Protection (2020)', suggesting a possible amendment; not verified - see backlog.

title: Instruction on the Implementation of the Law on Electronic Data Protection (No. 2126/MTC)
short_title: Instruction on Implementation of the Law on Electronic Data Protection
summary: Implementing instruction for the Law on Electronic Data Protection (No. 25/NA, 2017).
source_title: Multilaw Data Protection Guide: Laos (Tilleke & Gibbins)
notes: Number and date from the Tilleke & Gibbins guide; a second source confirms the instruction's existence but not its date. The instruction text itself was not checked.

title: Law on Cybersecurity (No. 87/NA)
issuer: National Assembly of the Lao PDR
summary: Sets principles, regulations and standards for the management and monitoring of cybersecurity; the Ministry of Technology and Communications is the central coordinating authority; defines critical national information infrastructure, establishes a National Cybersecurity Operations System, and requires cybersecurity incident reporting.
source_title: Rajah & Tann Asia, Regional Round-Up: Lao PDR Q1 2026
notes: National Assembly reviewed the draft on 23 June 2025 (KPL); law dated 25 June 2025 and published in the Lao Official Gazette on 20 March 2026. One LNTV Facebook post (8 Oct 2026) lists a 'Draft Law on Cyber Security' among items for the October 2026 NA session; this appears to mislabel the anti-cybercrime amendment and is not treated as contradicting Gazette publication.

title: National Strategy on Artificial Intelligence 2026-2035 (draft)
summary: Draft ten-year AI strategy; the Cabinet agreed it in principle at the September government meeting (22-23 Sep 2026) and instructed the Ministry of Technology and Communications to revise it, with greater focus on infrastructure, databases and personnel; the strategy is to be guided by UNESCO's AI Ethics Readiness Assessment (RAM) findings.
source_title: Asia News Network / Vientiane Times, 24 Sep 2026
next_milestone: Revised draft to return to Cabinet; no adoption date stated
notes: Agreement in principle reported 24 Sep 2026, following the government meeting of 22-23 Sep. Full strategy text is not public; no KPL report of the Cabinet decision was located. Corroborated by Laotian Times (via The Laos Briefing) and US-ASEAN.

title: Law on Anti-Cybercrime (Amended) (draft)
summary: Revises the 2015 cybercrime law for social media, artificial intelligence, digital financial services and cloud computing; 10 parts and 62 articles (49 revised, 12 new); Part II defines 12 cybercrime types including cyber fraud, unauthorised manipulation of digital content, dissemination of pornographic material through cyber channels and cyber-enabled violence against women and children; provides for a National Committee for Anti-Cybercrime and a 24-hour emergency response centre.
next_milestone: National Assembly adoption
notes: Presented by the MTC minister to the 2nd Ordinary Session of the 10th National Assembly; deliberations ongoing at time of reporting, not yet adopted. KPL is the state news agency (primary source).

title: Cybersecurity Law No. 1/2025
summary: Enacted 1 Jan 2025 and brought into force 30 Jul 2025 by SAC Notification 113/2025. Licences (3-10 years) for cybersecurity services and for digital platforms with over 100,000 users in Myanmar; platforms must retain user data up to 3 years and disclose it on written request; VPN services require ministry approval (1-6 months' imprisonment / MMK 1-10m fine for unapproved provision); extraterritorial reach over Myanmar citizens abroad; penalties for cyber misuse, online theft/mischief and unapproved online gambling. No AI-specific provisions were found in the law text or in law-firm summaries.
notes: FLAG: SAC-enacted law, legitimacy contested. No AI provisions: full-text search of the Lincoln Legal English translation for 'artificial' returned nothing. Implementing rules/licensing procedures had not been issued as of Sep 2026 (Search-Risk).

title: Electronic Transactions Law (2004), as amended 15 February 2021
summary: 2021 amendment added Chapter 10 on protection of personal information, including a broad Section 27-C exception allowing government access to personal data for cybersecurity/cybercrime matters relating to stability, tranquillity and national security, and Section 38-C criminalising creating false/fake news online with intent to cause public panic (1-3 years' imprisonment or fine up to MMK 10m). Myanmar has no standalone data-protection statute; this is the closest data-protection provision.
notes: SAC amendment, legitimacy contested. Status in_force is inferred (no repeal found); the 2025 Cybersecurity Law overlaps but does not expressly repeal the ET Law. No AI-specific provisions.

title: National AI Strategy and National AI Policy (2025-2030) [draft]
summary: Draft National AI Strategy and National AI Policy (2025-2030) under preparation by the Ministry of Science and Technology; fourth coordination meeting held in Nay Pyi Taw in February 2025, chaired by Union Minister Myo Thein Kyaw, aiming to integrate AI into development sectors, raise public awareness of AI ethics and standards, and align with the ASEAN Guide on AI Governance and Ethics. Awaits approval; no adoption date found.
next_milestone: Adoption check
notes: Date discrepancy: Straits AI says the meeting was 18 Feb; the Myanmar National Portal article cited by Safer Internet Lab is dated 19 Feb 2025 (likely publication date). I used 18 Feb. See backlog for an unverified claim that this strategy was issued/took effect 27 Feb 2026.

title: Cyber Security Policy 2023
issuer: Department of Information Technology and Cyber Security, Ministry of Transport and Communications
summary: Five-year strategic framework (to 2028) for a stable and robust cyber environment, prioritising enactment of cyber/digital security legislation, a Cyber Security Central Committee and Steering Committee, critical-information-infrastructure protection, digital certification and platform-service-provider registration, and cybercrime/cyber-fraud prevention. Precursor to the 2025 Cybersecurity Law.
next_milestone: Implementation progress check
notes: Secondary source (Digital Watch summary of the MoTC policy); I did not locate the full policy text. AI is mentioned only in passing in the surrounding GNLM coverage (AI's influence on mankind/society), not as a policy pillar.

title: Amendment to the Protection of Personal Privacy and Personal Security of Citizens Law 2025 (NDSC Law No. 1/2025)
summary: Enacted 1 Aug 2025; suspended Sections 5, 7 and 8 of the 2017 Law Protecting the Privacy and Security of Citizens — the protections against search/seizure/arrest without civilian witnesses, detention beyond 24 hours without a court order, and surveillance/interception of communications without a warrant — for the period the NDSC exercises legislative, executive and judicial powers.
source_title: Global New Light of Myanmar, 2 Aug 2025
notes: FLAG: NDSC/SAC instrument, legitimacy contested. Status superseded: NDSC Law 4/2026 (3 Feb 2026, see MM-P-06) replaced Section 5(b) and the Section 8 preamble. Date is inferred: GNLM dated 2 Aug 2025 says the NDSC 'yesterday enacted' the amendment, i.e. 1 Aug 2025.

title: Amendment to the Law Protecting the Privacy and Security of the Citizen (NDSC Law 4/2026)
summary: Replaced Section 5(b) (search/seizure/arrest of a residence to be in the presence of at least two witnesses, including a ward/village-tract administrator, except where urgently required for national defence, security or public peace) and the preamble of Section 8 (no search, surveillance or interception without an order, permission or warrant under existing law, or approval of the President/Union Government, except for persons vested with duties for national defence, security and public peace). Partially qualifies the 2021/2025 suspensions; the full consolidated position is unresolved.
source_title: Global New Light of Myanmar, 5 Feb 2026
notes: FLAG: NDSC/SAC instrument, legitimacy contested. GNLM published the text 5 Feb 2026; the law itself is dated 3 Feb 2026. Interaction between the 2021 suspension, the 2025 suspension and this 2026 amendment is not resolved in the sources I found.

title: Guide on Artificial Intelligence Governance and Ethics for Brunei Darussalam (first edition)
short_title: AI Governance and Ethics Guide (1st ed.)
summary: Voluntary, risk-based, technology- and sector-agnostic guide setting seven principles for organisations that design, develop, deploy or use AI: transparency and explainability; data protection and data governance; security and safety; robustness and reliability; fairness and equity; human centricity; and accountability and integrity. Developed by AITI with the AI Governance and Ethics Working Group, mirroring the ASEAN Guide on AI Governance and Ethics.
notes: Superseded by the second edition (BN-P-02, 2026).

title: Guide on Artificial Intelligence Governance and Ethics for Brunei Darussalam (second edition)
short_title: AI Governance and Ethics Guide (2nd ed.)
summary: Second edition of AITI's voluntary AI governance guide, expanded to cover generative AI risks and with concrete Bruneian use-case examples of responsible AI implementation; retains the seven principles of the first edition.
source_title: Authority for Info-communications Technology Industry (Instagram), 8 Apr 2026
notes: AITI's official Instagram announced the second edition on 8 Apr 2026; The Star reported it on 1 May 2026 ('Brunei ramps up efforts to ensure ethical AI practices') and LexLint dates the second edition to May 2026. Day-precision date follows AITI's own announcement; if the parent's convention prefers the press-report date, use 2026-05-01.

title: Personal Data Protection Order, 2025
summary: Comprehensive consent-based data-protection regime for private-sector organisations (S 1/2025), modelled on Singapore's PDPA: consent and purpose controls, access and correction rights, care of personal data, cross-border transfer, breach notification and offences, with a private right of action; administered and enforced by AITI. Does not apply to government agencies.
notes: Gazetted 8 Jan 2025 (S 1/2025). Parts 1, 2, 10 (excluding s.42), 11, 12 and Schedule 6 commenced 8 Jan 2025 (S 10/2025); Parts 3-9, s.42 and Schedules 1-5 commenced 1 Jan 2026 (S 11/2025). A one-year grace/sunrise period ran to January 2026.

title: Digital Brunei 2030: The Digital Brunei Transformation Plan — Data and Artificial Intelligence Strategy
issuer: Digital Brunei Council (Ministry of Transport and Infocommunications)
summary: Five-year national plan for digital growth to 2030, bringing together four strategies including a cross-cutting Data and Artificial Intelligence Strategy with four outcomes: accessible, high-quality, secure and well-governed data assets; a data-driven and AI-aware organisational culture; human capital for AI transformation; and effective use and deployment of AI. Flagship projects include an AI-capable data centre, a national sovereign cloud with AI compute, and a Brunei-context national large language model.
source_title: Ministry of Transport and Infocommunications, 2 Jun 2026
notes: Succeeds the Digital Economy Masterplan 2025 (BN-P-07).

title: Generative AI (GenAI) Guidance for Education — Handbook Edition
summary: National handbook for schools and educators on the responsible and ethical use of generative AI, covering digital safety, academic integrity, responsible AI use and personal data protection, with seven principles for ethical AI in education, tiers of AI use and an AI readiness pathway; aligned with Wawasan Brunei 2035 and the Ministry's Digital Transformation Plan 2023-2027.
source_title: Ministry of Education, GenAI Guidance for Education (handbook PDF)
notes: Month precision: TNBD reports a September 2025 launch; the handbook PDF is timestamped 18 Sep 2025 and its foreword says it was launched in conjunction with the National Teachers' Day celebration, whose conference events ran 8-9 Oct 2025 — the exact launch day is unverified.

title: Cybersecurity Act (Chapter 272)
summary: Legal framework to require or authorise measures to prevent, manage and respond to cybersecurity threats and incidents, and to regulate owners of critical information infrastructure (energy, info-communications, healthcare, banking and finance, defence and security, emergency services, aviation, government, media, water). Passed as the Cybersecurity Order on 20 May 2023 and became the Cybersecurity Act in 2024.
source_title: Cyber Security Brunei — Cybersecurity Act Chapter 272
notes: No AI- or deepfake-specific provision verified; included as the national cybersecurity framework under which AI-enabled cyber incidents are handled. Exact date it became an Act in 2024 unverified.

title: Constitution of the Democratic Republic of Timor-Leste, Section 38 — Protection of personal data
summary: Section 38 gives everyone the right to access personal data held about them and to know its purpose, and prohibits processing of sensitive data such as beliefs, religion, party or union membership or ethnic origin without consent; it states the law will define personal data and set rules, but no implementing data-protection law had been enacted as of 29 October 2026.
notes: Date is entry into force per Section 170 of the Constitution; Article 38 title and text confirmed via WIPO Lex. No comprehensive data-protection law in force — see TL-P-04.

title: Timor Digital 2032 — National Strategic Plan for Digital Development and Information and Communication Technology
summary: Ten-year national digital and ICT strategy launched 2 June 2023, covering e-government, inclusive economy, health, education and agriculture, with data protection and privacy among its principles; it contained no AI-specific provisions at launch, and UNESCO records it as being revised to formally incorporate AI.
source_title: Government of Timor-Leste — launch of Timor Digital 2032
next_milestone: Revised Timor Digital 2032 incorporating AI
notes: Confidence medium because the AI link rests on UNESCO's note that the strategy is being revised to incorporate AI; no revised text was found.

title: Draft Law on the Protection of Personal Data (Lei da Proteção de Dados Pessoais)
summary: Draft bill to establish a general personal-data protection framework and create an independent National Data Protection Authority (Autoridade Nacional de Proteção de Dados); a public consultation was held in July–August 2026, including a Ministry of Justice workshop on 31 July 2026; not enacted as of 1 November 2026.
source_title: Ministry of Justice — draft Personal Data Protection Law (mj.gov.tl)
next_milestone: Parliamentary submission and enactment
notes: Draft PDF text re-verified 20 Nov 2026 (mj.gov.tl, 52 pp., creates the ANPD as an independent authority). Date is month-precision (consultation month); the 1–30 August window reported by one weak source was not relied on. Not in force.

title: Proposal for legislative authorisation to approve a comprehensive cybersecurity legislative package
summary: Government proposal submitted to the National Parliament on 31 July 2026 (approved by the Council of Ministers 22 July 2026) seeking authority to adopt laws covering the National Cybersecurity Strategy, national cyberspace security, digital services, and criminal and criminal-procedural rules for digital-environment offences, including rules on personal data and privacy, digital-service-provider duties including notifying/removing/blocking illegal content, and a national cybersecurity authority.
next_milestone: Parliament decision on the authorisation
notes: No report found that Parliament had approved the authorisation as of 29 October 2026; status must be re-checked. Themes are data-protection and online-safety; no AI-specific provision was identified in the package description.

title: Digital Transformation Strategy 2026–2036 (draft)
summary: Draft national strategy presented for public consultation in Dili on 16–17 April 2026; pillars include digital governance, digital economy, digital education and skills, digital health, rural connectivity, cybersecurity, innovation and entrepreneurship, and the regulatory framework for emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence.
next_milestone: Publication of the final strategy
notes: Final version not found as of 29 October 2026 (per ZigmaNeural check); date is the first day of the consultation workshop.

title: Integrated National Plan to Prevent and Combat transnational digital financial fraud networks, supported by illicit online scam platforms (SCAM), organised cybercrime, and human trafficking, for 2026–2031
short_title: Integrated National Plan against digital financial fraud 2026–2031
issuer: Council of Ministers (proposal by Minister of the Interior Francisco da Costa Guterres)
summary: Government Resolution adopting an integrated national strategy against transnational digital financial fraud networks, illicit online scam platforms, organised cybercrime and human trafficking, with coordination across intelligence, security, criminal-investigation, financial and border agencies and a new National Centre for Coordination, Assessment, and Combating Transnational Threats (CN-CAT) reporting to the Prime Minister.
source_title: Government of Timor-Leste — Meeting of the Council of Ministers on August 5th, 2026
next_milestone: Implementation progress check
notes: No AI-specific element was identified in the Council communiqué; included as an online-safety / anti-scam instrument, not as AI-specific policy.

title: Prime Minister's Order No. 11/PM/VIII/2026 establishing the Interministerial Committee on Cybersecurity and the Digitalisation of State Services (CICDE)
issuer: Prime Minister Kay Rala Xanana Gusmão
summary: Order establishing the CICDE, chaired by the Minister of the Presidency of the Council of Ministers with the Minister of Transport and Communications as vice-chair, to coordinate cybersecurity, regulation of cyberspace, data protection, prevention and prosecution of cybercrime, and digitalisation of government services; it succeeds the Interministerial Cybersecurity Group established in October 2025.
notes: Order number and Jornal da República publication (Series II No. 31A, 6 August 2026) from the official gazette PDF record; the committee is a coordination body, so the parent may prefer to treat this as context rather than an instrument row.

title: Executive Order No. 131: Adopting the Artificial Intelligence Governance Framework and Creating the National Artificial Intelligence Council
short_title: EO 131 — AI Governance Framework and NAIC
summary: Adopts the AI Governance Framework for the Philippines as the national strategic guide for policy formulation, regulatory coordination, institutional development and capacity-building, built on four elements (ethics and principles; standards and assurance; risk-based policy toolkit; enabling resources). Creates the National Artificial Intelligence Council (NAIC), chaired by the Executive Secretary with the Secretary of Economy, Planning and Development as vice-chair, reporting directly to the President; the NAIC coordinates, facilitates and monitors implementation and reviews the framework at least every two years.
source_title: Executive Order No. 131, Official Gazette of the Philippines
next_milestone: First NAIC quarterly progress report to the President
notes: Signed 12 Nov 2026; effective 14 Nov 2026 upon publication in the Official Gazette. Missed by the 20 Nov 2026 update — dated before it, not a new development since 20 Nov.

title: NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC: Use of Real Persons' Likenesses in AI-Generated Images
summary: The NPC states a person's face and likeness are personal information under the Data Privacy Act (RA 10173), and photos and videos may also be biometric information; generating AI media from a real person's face or likeness and posting or sharing it is processing of personal data, which needs a legitimate purpose and a lawful basis (consent is the most recognisable but not the only basis). Without a lawful basis it may be unauthorised processing under Sec. 25, with criminal, civil and administrative liability. A fabricated image or video is false personal data; under Sec. 16(e) the person depicted may demand blocking, removal or destruction and complain to the NPC, which may investigate and issue compliance or cease-and-desist orders. Satire, parody and journalistic uses are recognised but only to the minimum extent necessary; the notice applies equally to public officials, and complaints involving minors get utmost priority.
notes: New instrument, not an update to PH-P-02: the Data Privacy Act itself is unchanged; this is a distinct 11 Aug 2026 NPC interpretive notice under RA 10173 Secs 3(g), 12, 16(e) and 25. No circular number and no separate compliance date. Title and date verified on the NPC's own site.

title: National Strategy on Artificial Intelligence to 2030, with a vision to 2045 (Decision No. 1671/QĐ-TTg)
summary: Approves a new national AI strategy to 2030 with a vision to 2045, replacing Decision 127/QĐ-TTg (2021). Shifts from AI research and application to economy-wide AI transformation. Targets include top-three ASEAN standing in AI R&D by 2030, top-ten in Asia by 2045, an AI economy of about 6% of GDP, about USD 5 billion in AI product and service exports, at least 10 Vietnamese AI brands, at least 8 Vietnamese-language AI models, and 100% of online public services integrated with AI.
source_title: Straits AI Institute — State of Applied AI: Vietnam
next_milestone: Implementation progress check
notes: Replaces Decision 127/QĐ-TTg; VN-P-04 marked superseded. Verified from several agreeing independents; the primary Vietnamese decision text was not retrieved in this session — fetch it on the next run. Missed by the 20 Nov 2026 update — dated before it, not a new development since 20 Nov.

title: AIPA Resolution on Strengthening Parliamentary Cooperation on AI Governance, Scientific Innovation and Ethical AI-Driven Growth in ASEAN
issuer: ASEAN Inter-Parliamentary Assembly (47th General Assembly, Manila)
summary: Merged resolution adopted at the 47th AIPA General Assembly in Manila, supporting parliamentary cooperation on AI governance, scientific innovation and ethical AI-driven growth. Operative paragraph 15 supports establishing an ASEAN AI Center in the Philippines, subject to ASEAN consensus and established processes.
next_milestone: ASEAN consensus decision on the proposed ASEAN AI Center
notes: The AIPA Economic Committee backed the proposal on 19 Nov 2026; the full Assembly adopted the merged resolution with 35 other resolutions at the closing plenary on 20 Nov 2026.

title: ASEAN–China Joint Statement on Commemorating the 5th Anniversary of the ASEAN-China Comprehensive Strategic Partnership
issuer: ASEAN Member States and China (29th ASEAN-China Summit, Manila)
summary: Joint statement marking five years of the ASEAN-China Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. Paragraphs 13–14 strengthen cooperation on AI, including AI safety and governance, welcome designating 2027 as the ASEAN-China Year of AI Cooperation, and acknowledge three ASEAN-China AI centres.
next_milestone: ASEAN-China Year of AI Cooperation, 2027
notes: Adopted at the 29th ASEAN-China Summit, Manila, 16 Nov 2026.

title: Scams (Countermeasures) and Other Matters Act 2026 (Act No. 21 of 2026)
summary: Omnibus anti-scam law passed 9 September 2026 and assented 24 September 2026. Gives police account-disabling orders (up to 30 days, one extension), disclosure orders and service-limitation orders (up to 3 years), and raises penalties for designated online services to S$10 million for code-of-practice and implementation-directive breaches. Amends the Online Criminal Harms Act so an anti-scam direction may be given by the operation of a computer program where the program assesses that an offence has been or is likely to be committed, or that online activity is preparatory to or in furtherance of a scam or malicious cyber activity offence.
source_title: Scams (Countermeasures) and Other Matters Act 2026 (Act No. 21 of 2026), Government Gazette
next_milestone: Commencement (date to be appointed by the Minister by Gazette notification)
notes: Status adopted, not in force: the Act comes into operation on a date the Minister appoints by notification in the Gazette. The statute itself says 'computer program'; commentary (fintechnews.sg) describes the program as using AI or machine learning. The Act names scam risk, not an AI risk — AI is the tool for issuing directions.

title: House Bill No. 10362: National AI Governance Act
summary: Comprehensive AI governance bill filed 29 July 2026 by Representatives Chel Diokno, Percival Cendaña, Dadah Kiram Ismula and Kaka Bag-ao. Would establish a national AI governance framework and an AI Bill of Rights (transparency, explanation, non-discrimination, human review, data protection, synthetic-media disclosure), require six months' notice, consultation and reskilling before high-impact systems displace workers, create a multi-stakeholder advisory council, and set penalties of six months to six years' imprisonment. Pending in the Committee on Information and Communications Technology since 3 August 2026.
source_title: AI Law Wiki — Philippines AI Law
next_milestone: Committee action in the House ICT Committee
notes: Status verified against AI Law Wiki (which cites the House listing) and multiple news reports; the House legislative status page itself was not read directly.

title: Governance Framework on the Use of Human-Centered Augmented Intelligence in the Philippine Judiciary (A.M. No. 25-11-28-SC)
issuer: Supreme Court of the Philippines (En Banc)
summary: En Banc resolution adopting a governance framework for human-centered augmented intelligence in the judiciary. Applies to judges, court officials and employees, court users (including lawyers) and vendors supplying AI tools to the judiciary. AI must augment, not replace, human judgment: it may not be the sole, primary or determinative basis for any adjudicatory outcome, and all legal reasoning must be independently formed by the human decision-maker. Sets principles of human-centered use, human rights, fairness, transparency, accountability, human oversight, privacy and data protection, security and sustainability, and creates a permanent Committee on Human-Centered Augmented Intelligence. Implemented through OCA Circular No. 47-2026 (11 Mar 2026).
next_milestone: Committee on Human-Centered Augmented Intelligence guidance and tool approvals
notes: Only Scriptix voice-to-text transcription was the AI application allowed as of a 1 July 2026 briefing; other applications require approval.

title: BSP Memorandum No. M-2026-031: Governance Principles for Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Financial Services
summary: Guidance paper setting out the BSP’s minimum supervisory expectations for AI adoption by BSP-supervised financial institutions. Built around five principles — Sustainability, Transparency, Accountability, Responsibility and Security (STARS) — applied across the AI system lifecycle (plan, develop, validate, deploy, monitor) and extended to outsourced service providers under a shared-responsibility model. Voluntary and non-binding.
next_milestone: BSP Model Risk Management Framework (forthcoming)
notes: Signed by Deputy Governor Lyn I. Javier, 24 June 2026. The memo notes the forthcoming Model Risk Management framework will address algorithmic fairness and model risks.
